headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: unstructured can read/write files and egress allowlisted data, while awesome-production-machine-learning is a non-runnable docs-only list with no execution surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default instruction-bridging channel is shown. agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b can read/write files but no shared filesystem or clipboard bridge between them is documented. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies agent_a output into files that agent_b parses as instructions, the risk becomes plausible.
IF both agents are mounted on the same shared workspace, reassess for injection via file content.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Require provenance tags on any content passed between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b can read files and send data to allowlisted network endpoints, while agent_a is a docs-only artifact with no data classes touched. There is no evidence of shared sensitive data, but if both are pointed at the same workspace, agent_b could exfiltrate document contents. Uncertainty remains, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem containing sensitive documents, leakage becomes plausible.
IF agent_b is configured to process files from the same directory as agent_a artifacts, document contents may flow to external APIs.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive sample files.
Disable network egress for agent_b during tests.
Review allowlisted endpoints before processing real documents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or runtime capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. agent_b can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but without a second writer there is no meaningful conflict pathway. The only plausible overlap is operational, not concurrent mutation.
conditions: IF another writable agent is added to the same directory, write conflicts become possible.
IF agent_a is replaced by a runnable component with filesystem writes, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Keep agent_a as a read-only reference artifact.
Serialize any agent_b writes to a dedicated directory.
Avoid sharing git state or mutable caches.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can process documents and act on outputs, so if it consumes agent_a-derived content as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream document handling. agent_a itself is not runnable and provides no verification layer, so the pair lacks an intrinsic check. The pathway exists only through orchestration, hence medium.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative input, cascading errors can propagate.
IF downstream actions are triggered from parsed document results without human review, impact increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before acting on outputs.
Require schema validation on any agent_a-derived text.
Log and diff intermediate outputs before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive data class or residency mismatch is documented for agent_a, and agent_b lists documents/images/text with allowlisted egress plus privacy-policy references. Because the pair lacks explicit regulated-data handling, compliance risk is limited to policy mismatch if sensitive documents are introduced later.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed by agent_b, compliance review is required.
IF agent_b's allowlisted endpoints differ from the operator's retention policy, reassess.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pairing.
Confirm retention and deletion settings before use.
Review the privacy policy links for the target deployment.
